headline: Asia: 8 killed in Ukraine as Russia hits back after Crimea bridge attacks
script:
Good evening. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- Asia: 8 killed in Ukraine as Russia hits back after Crimea bridge attacks.
- Africa: Sudan: Amnesty Calls for RSF Drone Attacks On Civilians in North Kordofan to Be Investigated As War Crimes.
- South Asia: On North Waziristan visit, CDF Munir vows to eliminate terrorism, preserve peace in KP.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: Renowned Iraq War Marine under federal investigation.
- Military Times, 5 hours ago: Renowned Iraq War Marine under federal investigation.
Retired Marine Sgt. Maj. Bradley Kasal is under investigation by the Naval Criminal Investigative Service for allegations over his conduct as an instructor for the Junior Reserve Officers' Training Corps.
The Caribbean - bottom line: Dereliction of duty - MoBay Chamber president warns owners of idle properties against holding city’s development hostage.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 2 days ago: Dereliction of duty - MoBay Chamber president warns owners of idle properties against holding city’s development hostage.
Property owners sitting on derelict buildings in Montego Bay, St James, are being urged to invest in their properties or sell them, as business and civic leaders push to transform the western city into what they envision as the Caribbean’s next capital. In a blunt warning, Jason Russell, president of the Montego Bay Chamber of Commerce and Industry, said prime properties in high-visibility tourism and entertainment areas could no longer be allowed to remain idle while the country pursues economic growth.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

SOUTH AMERICA
South America - bottom line: ‘Minefield’ returns for nine nights of memory, theater and reflection.
- Buenos Aires Herald, 13 hours ago: ‘Minefield’ returns for nine nights of memory, theater and reflection.
Lola Arias’ production featuring Argentine and British Malvinas War veterans premiered as part of the Herald’s 150th anniversary celebrations La entrada ‘Minefield’ returns for nine nights of memory, theater and reflection se publicó primero en Buenos Aires Herald.

EUROPE
Western Russia - bottom line: Russia launches ballistic missile attack on central Kryvyi Rih: child and paramedic killed, at least 21 injured.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 4 hours ago: Russia launches ballistic missile attack on central Kryvyi Rih: child and paramedic killed, at least 21 injured.
Russian forces attacked the centre of Kryvyi Rih with ballistic missiles on the evening of 20 November, injuring at least 21 people. A seven-year-old boy and a female paramedic have been killed in the attack.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 13 hours ago: Russia strikes emergency hospital in Kharkiv, damaging MRI scan room – photos.
Russian forces have attacked an emergency hospital in Kharkiv. A Russian drone has struck a room housing an MRI scanner. The scanner appears to have remained intact, but specialists will assess whether it is still functioning properly.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 14 hours ago: France calls for UN Security Council meeting over Russian strikes on Kyiv and embassies.
France is calling for a meeting of the UN Security Council following a series of Russian strikes on Ukraine that killed civilians in Kyiv and damaged the diplomatic missions of Austria and the Netherlands.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 14 hours ago: Child casualties from war in Ukraine reach highest level in almost four years – UNICEF.
UNICEF has reported that 114 children were killed and 1,030 injured in Ukraine between January and October 2026 – the highest child casualty figures in almost four years.
Southern Europe - bottom line: Latvian leader calls for closure of EU borders to all Russians.
- Politico Europe, 11 hours ago: Latvian leader calls for closure of EU borders to all Russians.
Andris Kulbergs warned that Europe cannot screen hundreds of thousands of Russian tourists as Moscow escalates its hybrid attacks.
- Politico Europe, 15 hours ago: Tusk: Russian cruise missile incursion into Poland seems ‘intentional’.
“This doesn’t look like an accident,” the Polish prime minister warned.
- Politico Europe, 16 hours ago: German defense minister apologizes for calling US criticism of Ukraine strikes ‘stupid’.
Boris Pistorius walked back his choice of words but stood by his support for Ukrainian strikes inside Russia.
- Balkan Insight, 10 hours ago: Republika Srpska Ban on 1990s Bosnian Army Symbols Ruled Unconstitutional.
The state-level Constitutional Court ruled against Republika Srpska’s law changes introducing prison terms for displaying flags or symbols of the Bosniak-led 1990s wartime army that fought against Serb forces.

AFRICA
Africa - bottom line: Sudan: Amnesty Calls for RSF Drone Attacks On Civilians in North Kordofan to Be Investigated As War Crimes.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 23 hours ago: Sudan: Amnesty Calls for RSF Drone Attacks On Civilians in North Kordofan to Be Investigated As War Crimes.
[Dabanga] El Obeid -- Amnesty International has called for an investigation into possible war crimes after documenting nine Rapid Support Forces (RSF) drone strikes that killed at least 37 civilians and injured 10 others in and around El Obeid, North Kordofan, between June and August 2026. The organisation's secretary general, Agnès Callamard, has urged the United Nations and African Union to take immediate action to protect civilians, including considering the deployment of an international protection force in Sudan.
- Africanews, 17 hours ago: Ukraine: Kyiv metro stations become overnight shelters amid air raids.
Residents of Kyiv, Ukraine, sought refuge in underground metro stations overnight on Thursday 19 November 2026, as repeated air raid alerts warned of further Russian attacks on the capital. Strikes on the Ukrainian capital killed at least one person, injured five and damaged two embassies.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 23 hours ago: Sudan: Sudan Drone Strikes 'Acts of Genocide' - Women's Rights Group.
[Dabanga] Amsterdam -- Sudanese women's rights group The No to Oppression against Women Initiative has condemned the continuation of the war in Sudan and the escalating use of drones against civilian-populated areas, including hospitals, schools, and electricity and water facilities, describing the attacks as "acts of genocide" against the Sudanese people.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 23 hours ago: Sudan: 10 Killed As Drone Strafes South Kordofan Gold Mine.
[Dabanga] South Kordofan -- At least 10 people have been killed and several others injured in a drone strike on the Bajoun mining site in Gadeer locality, South Kordofan, on Wednesday, according to witnesses. The UN confirms that Attacks on gold mining areas are linked to the war economy, with the deliberate targeting of sites with economic value to the opposing side.
Persian Gulf Region - bottom line: Saudi Arabia says it intercepts three Houthi missiles targeting Riyadh.
- Jerusalem Post, NDTV - Top Stories, Al Jazeera - Middle East, The Hindu - International, just now: Saudi Arabia says it intercepts three Houthi missiles targeting Riyadh.
Saudi Arabia intercepted three Houthi ballistic missiles targeting Riyadh, days after an attack damaged the capital's tallest skyscraper, as cross-border strikes intensify.
- Jerusalem Post, 4 hours ago: IDF strikes Hamas terror meeting in Gaza, one suspect killed in West Bank incident.
IDF forces and local security responded to the incident in the West Bank. A local security coordinator fired into the air before aiming at one of the suspects, who died as a result, the army said.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 7 hours ago: Israeli drone attacks kill seven Palestinians in central Gaza.
Drones cause 'fear and panic' among Palestinians as Israel continues attacks on the Strip despite 'ceasefire'.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, The Hindu - International, 7 hours ago: Russia complains of ‘new Iron Curtain’ as Estonia shuts its borders.
Tallinn's decision to shut road border crossings comes after an attack on a drone manufacturer.
South Africa - bottom line: South Africa: Joburg Residents Could Face R120,000 Fine for Watering the Lawn.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 10 hours ago: South Africa: Joburg Residents Could Face R120,000 Fine for Watering the Lawn.
[Daily Maverick] When the clock strikes midnight on Friday, 20 November, Johannesburg residents might want to revise their budgets, further limit their shower time and find alternative sources to municipal water as level 2 restrictions hit.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 14 hours ago: South Africa: Cachalia Drops Apartheid Truth Bombs As Latest Stats Show '60 Killed Daily in SA'.
[Daily Maverick] South Africa's latest official crime statistics show that over three months, 5,590 people were murdered in the country. Referencing gang killings and violence, Acting Police Minister Firoz Cachalia reminded Parliamentarians that apartheid's legacy still affected these crimes and that the most affected areas needed development, not just heightened policing.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 10 hours ago: South Africa: Gbvf Policy Promises Must Turn Into Daily Safety for Women - Deputy President.
[SAnews.gov.za] South Africa must move beyond policy promises and awareness campaigns to deliver real protection for the more than one in three women who still face physical or sexual violence in their lifetime.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 15 hours ago: South Africa: North-West Mother Pleads for Help After Daughter Loses Both Legs.
[Scrolla] Pauline Mhlongo says she stays on her feet through the night when it rains because their shack leaks. Former ward councillor Andrew Zimba says the family's unfinished three-bedroom house still needs a roof.

ASIA
Asia - bottom line: 8 killed in Ukraine as Russia hits back after Crimea bridge attacks.
- South China Morning Post - China, NDTV - Top Stories, Africanews, The Moscow Times, The Hindu - International, 3 hours ago: 8 killed in Ukraine as Russia hits back after Crimea bridge attacks.
Russia launched one of the largest missile and drone attacks of the war on Ukraine on Friday, pummelling electricity facilities and killing eight people, after President Vladimir Putin vowed to retaliate for Ukrainian attacks on a bridge to Crimea. Overnight strikes on the three bridges in Kyiv that cross the Dnipro River and link the two sides of the capital were the biggest of Russia’s war in Ukraine. Residents ‌took shelter in the metro as dozens of explosions echoed around the...
- South China Morning Post - China, 4 hours ago: Russian missiles land in Poland, as Europe holds military drills nearby.
Two Russian missiles and a suspected drone came down in Poland on Friday in what its prime minister said was likely to be a provocation timed to coincide with European military exercises in his country for a possible post-war mission in Ukraine. The incidents occurred while Russia carried out a major nighttime bombardment of neighbouring Ukraine. The development stoked tensions between Europe and Moscow just as the US is trying to add momentum to talks it is mediating on ending the war that...
- South China Morning Post - China, 6 hours ago: Can China’s top-down military adapt to the speed of AI and drone warfare?.
Drawing on lessons from the Ukraine war, Chinese military commentators are calling for frontline commanders to have greater freedom to make battlefield decisions without waiting for orders from above, as drones and AI accelerate the pace of combat. Since July, several commentaries in the PLA Daily, the People’s Liberation Army’s official newspaper, have proposed ways to delegate tactical authority while keeping major military operations under centralised command. This type of flexibility...
- South China Morning Post - China, 13 hours ago: Concrete aims or just symbolism? Trump, Xi and Putin talk nuclear risk but controls stall.
The joint pledge to reduce nuclear risk by the United States, China and Russia during their unprecedented three-way summit this week sends a positive signal on stability, analysts say, although they warn that there is little room for optimism without concrete measures. Nuclear arms control among the world’s three major nuclear powers – long sought by US President Donald Trump – failed to make it into the joint declaration after his talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President...
South Asia - bottom line: On North Waziristan visit, CDF Munir vows to eliminate terrorism, preserve peace in KP.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 15 hours ago: On North Waziristan visit, CDF Munir vows to eliminate terrorism, preserve peace in KP.
Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir reaffirmed on Friday the security force’s “unwavering resolve” to decisively eliminate terrorism and preserve peace and stability of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa in close coordination with law enforcement agencies (LEAs). The CDF said this during a visit to Miranshah in KP’s North Waziristan, the military media wing said in a statement.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 9 hours ago: CTD says 3 terrorists, including mastermind of Kohat police lines attack, killed in IBO.
PESHAWAR: The Counter Terrorism Department (CTD) on Friday claimed to have killed three terrorists of the banned Ittehadul Mujahideen Pakistan (IMP), including the mastermind of the Kohat Police Lines attack in September. The three were killed in an intelligence-based operation (IBO) carried out in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Kohat, following information about presence of the group members in the area, a CTD statement said. According to an official statement, the Kohat CTD received intelligence that armed terrorists of the banned IMP had set up a checkpoint on Bazeed Khel Road in Kohat.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 14 hours ago: FO rejects India's 'undiplomatic, irresponsible' remarks about Pakistan's mineral wealth.
The Foreign Office (FO) on Friday categorically rejected the “undiplomatic and irresponsible” remarks made by India at the United Nations regarding the country’s mineral wealth. At the UN Security Council (UNSC) Arria-formula meeting on natural resources and conflict, on Thursday India’s Permanent Representative to the UN Ambassador Parvathaneni Harish had “directly accused the Pakistan military of looting the country’s natural resources for personal gain and triggering domestic political turmoil to keep control over them”, according to Indian news agency ANI.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 22 hours ago: Pakistan 'unequivocally' condemns Houthi attack on Riyadh’s tallest skyscraper.
Pakistan on Friday “unequivocally” condemned a Houthi attack on Riyadh’s tallest skyscraper, which serves as the headquarters of Saudi Arabia’s sovereign wealth fund. “This act of aggression constitutes a grave violation of the sovereignty of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia,” the Foreign Office (FO) said in a statement condemning Thursday’s attack, without naming the tower. Saudi state-run news agency SPA reported, citing the kingdom’s civil defence, that the attack caused material damage to several floors of the building and nearby buildings, but no injuries were reported.
India - bottom line: Russian missiles, drone crash in Poland near Nato drills; Warsaw flags provocation.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 3 hours ago: Russian missiles, drone crash in Poland near Nato drills; Warsaw flags provocation.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 3 hours ago: Magnitude 6.8 earthquake strikes central Peru, tremors felt in Lima.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 2 hours ago: No China input yet on GoPro cam used during Pahalgam terror attack: NIA.
NIA director general Rakesh Aggarwal reported that a GoPro camera linked to the Pahalgam attack, which resulted in 26 fatalities including 25 tourists, remains unclaimed by China. This camera was lost in July 2025 when authorities neutralized the terrorists. Meanwhile, allegations by Mathew VanDyke regarding his treatment in custody haven’t been addressed in court. The investigation into the camera's origins continues as officials await China's response.
- Times of India - Top Stories, one hour ago: Adani project work on at village not listed in clearance: Official.
Adani Green Energy Ltd's Tarali pumped storage project is under investigation due to alleged unauthorized work at Sawarghar. Concerns have been raised regarding approvals from the National Board for Wildlife and environmental clearances. The Maharashtra Pollution Control Board is looking into these allegations and has conducted inspections. An honorary wildlife warden has requested a detailed inquiry into the project's compliance with regulations.
Korean Peninsula - bottom line: Trump, Xi and Putin discuss North Korea, nuclear risks at first trilateral talks.
- NK News, 21 hours ago: Trump, Xi and Putin discuss North Korea, nuclear risks at first trilateral talks.
The leaders of the U.S., China and Russia pledged to pursue greater cooperation on nuclear nonproliferation at their first-ever trilateral summit on Thursday, while also discussing regional security issues and the Korean Peninsula. After the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen, U.S. President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin […]

AUSTRALIA
Australia - bottom line: Australia-wide rallies warn freebirths will soar under new rules.
- ABC News Australia, one hour ago: Australia-wide rallies warn freebirths will soar under new rules.
Dozens of rallies are being held in cities and towns across the country, warning new insurance rules will lead to a "catastrophic collapse" in access to midwife-supported homebirths.
- ABC News Australia, 4 hours ago: Man convicted of starting deadly 2025 LA Palisades Fire.
Jonathan Rinderknecht is found guilty at his second trial of sparking last year's deadly Palisades Fire, which killed 12 people.
- The Guardian - Australia, 14 hours ago: Anthony Albanese didn’t dazzle on the world stage, but he didn’t miss when he challenged Vladimir Putin.
The prime minister’s flourish-free, middle-power ethos guided his classic performance on this major foreign policy trip Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast For days leading up to this week’s Apec leaders’ summit, Anthony Albanese said he wouldn’t miss the opportunity to tell Vladimir Putin what he thought of the war in Ukraine. Battling a persistent lurgy across 11 days, during which he visited three countries and endless meeting rooms, the prime minister faced criticism for posing alongside the Russian leader in the summit “family photo” in Shenzhen.
- The Guardian - Australia, 23 hours ago: Kellie Sloane says she’s ‘pretty sure’ NSW Liberals exodus is over after Mark Speakman resigns.
Former opposition leader warns party against being ‘One Nation lite’ as he becomes eighth out of 24 Liberal MPs not to recontest seat in March Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast The New South Wales opposition leader, Kellie Sloane, says she is “pretty sure” the exodus of Liberals before the March state election has finished, after Mark Speakman became the eighth MP to decide not to recontest their lower house seats.

This briefing is compiled automatically from regional news feeds and has not been cross-referenced by an editor. Treat single-source claims as unconfirmed. I will be back with the next update.
